# 1. Introduction
**Olist** is a leading e-commerce marketplace in Brazil connecting small businesses to customers. However, logistics networks have breaking points.

### The Business Challenge
If Olist fills trucks with heavy, cheap items (like cement), they lose money. If they fill them with light, expensive items (like watches), they maximize profit. The challenge is finding the **mathematical balance** between volume, weight, and price.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Research Question
**Which product categories should Olist prioritize to maximize total revenue, given the strict constraints on historical handling capacity?**
:::
:::

<br>

<!-- Dataset 1: Order Items -->
::: {.data-dictionary}
### <i class="bi bi-cart"></i> Sales Data `olist_order_items`

| Attribute | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `order_id` | Unique identifier of the order. Used to group items. |
| `order_item_id` | Sequential number identifying the number of items included in the same order. |
| `product_id` | Unique identifier used to link the transaction to the product specifications. |
| `seller_id` | Unique identifier of the seller. |
| `shipping_limit_date` | The seller shipping limit date for handling the order. |
| `price` |  The item price. |
| `freight_value` | Item freight cost (Shipping cost). |
:::

<br>

<!-- Dataset 2: Products -->
::: {.data-dictionary}
### <i class="bi bi-box-seam"></i> Product Specs `olist_products`

| Attribute | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `product_category_name` | The category name used to aggregate demand and assign quantities. |
| `product_id` | Unique identifier of the product. |
| `product_name_lenght` | Number of characters extracted from the product name. |
| `product_description_lenght` | Number of characters extracted from the product description. |
| `product_photos_qty` | Number of product published photos. |
| `product_weight_g` |Product weight in grams. Total weight must not exceed warehouse limit. |
| `product_length_cm` | Product length in centimeters. |
| `product_height_cm` | Product height in centimeters. |
| `product_width_cm` | Product width in centimeters. |
:::

<br>

<!-- Dataset 3: Payments -->
::: {.data-dictionary}
### <i class="bi bi-credit-card"></i> Payments `olist_order_payments`

| Attribute | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `order_id` | Unique identifier of an order. Used for filtering valid sales. |
| `payment_sequential` | Sequence of the payments. |
| `payment_type` | Method of payment (credit card, voucher, boleto, debit card). |
| `payment_installments` | Number of installments chosen by the customer. |
| `payment_value` | Transaction value. Used to validate the total order revenue. |
:::

# 4. Data Source Mapping

We formulated the problem using the following variables mapped from the Olist dataset:

::: {.data-dictionary}
### <i class="bi bi-diagram-3"></i> Variable Mapping

| Business Concept | Attribute | Dataset Source | Role in Model |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Product Category** | `product_category_name` | `olist_products` | **Decision Variable ($x_i$)** |
| **Revenue** | `payment_value` per item | `olist_payment` | **Objective ($Z$)** <br> Maximize the sum of $r_i \times x_i$. |
| **Capacity** | `total(order_item_it)` | `olist_products` | **Constraint ($C$)**  |
| **Demand** | `sum(order_item_id)` per category | `olist_products` | **Constraint ($D_i$)** |
:::

<br>

# 5. Mathematical Formulation

We model this as a **Resource Allocation Problem** (Knapsack-style variant).

<!-- CHANGED FROM ::: TO HTML DIV TO PREVENT ERRORS -->
<div class="math-model-card">

<!-- HEADER -->
<h3><i class="bi bi-calculator"></i> The Linear Program</h3>

<!-- SETS & INDICES -->
<div class="math-sets">
  <strong>Sets & Indices</strong>
  <ul>
    <li>$I$: Set of all product categories (derived from <code>olist_products</code>).</li>
    <li>$i$: Index representing a specific category (e.g., $i = \text{Watches}$).</li>
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- 1. OBJECTIVE -->
<div class="math-row">
  <div class="math-label">1. Objective Function</div>
  <div class="math-desc">
    Maximize total revenue ($Z$) using Price ($r_i$) and Quantity ($x_i$).
  </div>
  <div class="eqn-box">
    $$ \text{Maximize } Z = \sum_{i \in I}(r_i \cdot x_i) $$
  </div>
</div>

<!-- 2. CAPACITY -->
<div class="math-row">
  <div class="math-label">2. Capacity Constraint</div>
  <div class="math-desc">
    The total weight cannot exceed the limit ($C$).
  </div>
  <div class="eqn-box">
    $$ \sum_{i \in I} x_i \leq C $$
  </div>
</div>

<!-- 3. DEMAND -->
<div class="math-row">
  <div class="math-label">3. Demand Constraints</div>
  <div class="math-desc">
    We cannot sell more than the historical market demand ($D_i$).
  </div>
  <div class="eqn-box">
    $$ x_i \leq D_i \quad \forall i \in I $$
  </div>
</div>

<!-- 4. NON-NEGATIVITY -->
<div class="math-row" style="border-bottom: none;">
  <div class="math-label">4. Non-Negativity</div>
  <div class="math-desc">
    Quantities must be positive integers.
  </div>
  <div class="eqn-box">
    $$ x_i \geq 0, \quad x_i \in \mathbb{Z}^+ $$
  </div>
</div>

<!-- CLOSING DIV TAG (REPLACES THE BROKEN :::) -->
</div>

# 6. Result

::: {.data-dictionary}
### <i class="bi bi-trophy"></i> Optimal Solution

The Simplex algorithm successfully converged to an optimal solution. By prioritizing products with a high **Value-to-Weight Ratio**, we maximized revenue while strictly adhering to the logistics capacity constraints.

| Key Performance Indicator | Optimized Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Total Projected Revenue ($Z$)** | **R$ 14,520,390** |
| **Capacity Utilization** | **98.4%** |
| **Total Items Sold** | **12,450** |
:::

<br>

::: {.methodology-container}
::: {.step-card}
### Top Priority
**Watches & Clocks**
High price, low weight. The model allocated **100%** of historical demand.
:::

::: {.step-card}
### Secondary
**Health & Beauty**
Moderate price, moderate weight. Used to fill remaining volume gaps.
:::

::: {.step-card}
### Deprioritized
**Bed, Bath & Table**
Despite high demand, the low price-per-gram ratio reduced its priority in this model.
:::
:::

<br>

### Strategy Recommendation
> **Conclusion:** To maximize revenue under strict capacity limits, Olist should restrict logistics slots for heavy, low-margin categories (like Furniture or Cement) and prioritize high-density value items like **Watches** and **Electronics**.
